mintAuthority.summary: KRWQ's canonical Ethereum token is a TransparentUpgradeableProxy over a Frax-style ERC20 with an owner-managed minter set: minterMint(address,uint256) is uncapped for any address in the minters mapping, and the owner (3/5 Safe 0x56398b89) can addMinter/removeMinter at will. Two active minters are KRWTCustodianWithOracle contracts, both owned by that same Safe. Base, Polygon and Fraxtal do not run lock/unlock adapters: each is a native mint-and-burn LayerZero OFT (KRWQOFT is OFTUpgradeable; token() returns itself and approvalRequired() is false), so its owner Safe can setPeer a new trusted remote and cause unbounded KRWQ to be credited on that chain. Every deployment is a transparent proxy; on Ethereum and Base the ProxyAdmin is owned by the chain's Safe, but on Polygon and Fraxtal the ProxyAdmin is owned by a single EOA (0x9fEAB70f), which can replace the implementation unilaterally. Codex and Morph are note-only (no public RPC).

controls.label: KRWQ Ethereum owner (3/5 Safe)
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25530913: KRWQ (0xc00db6b4) is a transparent proxy (EIP-1967 impl 0x350b6b5c, ProxyAdmin 0xff85d94f). Verified implementation source: contract KRWQ is ERC20Permit, ERC20Burnable, Ownable2Step, with minterMint(address,uint256) onlyMinters (calls _mint, no cap) and addMinter/removeMinter onlyOwner. owner() = Safe 0x56398b89, pendingOwner() = zero. ProxyAdmin.owner() = the same Safe. mintersArray enumerates 2 active minters, 0x5573b8db and 0x7e88ac6a, both verified KRWTCustodianWithOracle proxies whose owner() and ProxyAdmin.owner() are also Safe 0x56398b89. Safe state: getThreshold()=3, getOwners()=5, getModulesPaginated() empty, guard slot zero.
controls.capDescription: No cap. minterMint(address,uint256) is uncapped for any address in the minters mapping; addMinter(address)/removeMinter(address) are onlyOwner, so this Safe can authorize unbounded new KRWQ on the canonical chain. It also owns the Ethereum ProxyAdmin.

controls.label: KRWQ Polygon ProxyAdmin owner (single EOA)
controls.capDescription: Single-key upgrade authority. As sole owner of the Polygon ProxyAdmin (0x4583b85c), this EOA can call upgradeAndCall() to replace the KRWQ implementation with one that mints without limit. No cap, no timelock, no multisig.
controls.evidence: At Polygon block 90218312: the KRWQ proxy's EIP-1967 admin slot holds ProxyAdmin 0x4583b85c (OZ v5: upgradeAndCall(address,address,bytes) onlyOwner, UPGRADE_INTERFACE_VERSION present). ProxyAdmin.owner() = 0x9feab70f, and eth_getCode at that address returned 0x (no code) — a plain EOA, not a Safe. This address is also a signer on all four KRWQ Safes.

review.evidence: Re-verified on-chain at pinned blocks (Ethereum 25530913, Base 48621557/48621722, Polygon 90218312/90218531, Fraxtal 38610876/38611041). All four deployments are TransparentUpgradeableProxies. Ethereum: owner() = 3/5 Safe 0x56398b89 (owners and threshold re-read, no modules, guard zero); implementation KRWQ exposes uncapped minterMint() onlyMinters plus addMinter/removeMinter onlyOwner; mintersArray = 2 active KRWTCustodianWithOracle contracts, both owned by that Safe; ProxyAdmin 0xff85d94f owned by that Safe. Base/Polygon/Fraxtal are NOT lock/unlock adapters: each implementation is KRWQOFT is OFTUpgradeable with token() == self and approvalRequired() == false (native mint/burn OFT), so each owner Safe can setPeer a new trusted remote and cause unbounded credit-side minting on its chain; canRaiseCap is therefore true for all three. ProxyAdmin ownership is split: Ethereum and Base ProxyAdmins are owned by their chain Safe, but the Polygon (0x4583b85c) and Fraxtal (0x3faff366) ProxyAdmins are owned by a single EOA, 0x9feab70f (eth_getCode = 0x on both chains), which can unilaterally replace the implementation. Codex and Morph remain note-only (no public RPC). Economic-posture fields reviewed 2026-08-15: issuer-controlled Safes and EOAs can add minters, trust new OFT peers, or replace mint logic without a timelock; the assets-only Chainlink feed does not reconcile global liabilities and no supervisor or independent attestor is evidenced. Wave 2 external review 2026-08-15: the live issuer page displays aggregate minted KRWQ and reserve assets, but the whitepaper still describes independent attestations as planned and neither source proves liability coverage for every native OFT and unresolved deployment.
